A1.justification: Both PDFs describe FloorplanQA. The complete main texts and appendices are readable, including tables, figures and equations. Content can be matched reliably across the added sections and renumbering.

before.justification: v3 reports original evaluations of 15 LLMs on 2,000 layouts and 16,000 questions, alongside tool, visual-input and robustness experiments.

after.justification: v4 retains the original benchmark evaluations and adds visual-input experiments, layout-complexity correlations and inference-resource measurements.

M1.justification: The layout-generation pipeline, symbolic representation, question templates, geometric reference computations and scoring procedures remain unchanged. The additional rendering conditions extend evaluation rather than revise the underlying benchmark method.

E1.justification: v3 tests symbolic inputs and images accompanied by JSON. v4 substantially broadens input scenarios with image-only evaluation and photorealistic generated images, requiring geometry to be recovered visually. The eight tasks and underlying layout domains remain; the newly named Mixed sample does not establish a new source dataset.

E2.justification: The main 15-model comparison is unchanged. The expanded VLM comparison adds GPT-5-mini and Gemini 3.1 FL alongside GPT-4.1-mini. Conversely, v3 Table 8's GPT-4.1-mini tool/rendering comparison columns are absent from the corresponding v4 Table 10, which retains GPT-4.1.

E3.justification: v4 adds a seven-condition comparison on 200 Mixed rooms: JSON-only and three rendering styles each with and without JSON. Appendix E also introduces per-layout analysis averaging 15 models and seven tasks, with paths analyzed separately. These substantially extend the evaluation design; existing benchmark budgets and scoring settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Beyond v3's rendering tests and single-model HSSD free-space complexity curve, v4 adds systematic rendering/JSON ablations and full-dataset complexity correlations, task-specific associations and waypoint analysis. These substantially expand evidence about input dependence and sources of difficulty. Existing tolerance, semantic and case-study analyses are retained.

E5.justification: v4 Table 6 introduces Spearman correlations with significance reporting over 2,000 layouts, including p < 10^-137 for overlap count. v3 has no corresponding inferential analysis. No increased repeated-run count or new evaluation-seed reporting is documented.

E6.justification: Retained benchmark and GPT-4.1 tool scores match. Substantial new results include GPT-5-mini's 81.38% JSON-only, 83.81% Boxes+JSON and 20.06% Icons-only accuracy in Table 3, complexity correlations in Table 6, and resource measurements in Table 9. Earlier GPT-4.1-mini tool/rendering result entries are removed.

T1.justification: The geometric constraints, task definitions and mathematical reference computations are retained across the corresponding appendices. The new correlation analysis is empirical; it introduces no revised mathematical definition, derivation or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same central claims: a structured spatial-reasoning benchmark, 2,000 layouts, eight tasks, and persistent geometric and planning failures among evaluated LLMs. Additional analyses support these claims without redefining the core contribution.

C2.justification: v4 extends the visual-input interpretation to JSON dominance, object-label alignment and possible visual distraction. Appendix E distinguishes global tasks' complexity sensitivity from local-pair tasks and proposes difficulty control through layout selection. These refine v3's existing explanations of complexity and selective visual benefits.

D1.justification: v4 adds a project-page link, identifies Gemini 3.1 Flash Image and image-to-image generation for photorealistic inputs, and discloses token usage, provider/pricing assumptions and estimated inference costs in Appendix F.3. These are additional access and implementation disclosures, not changes to retained inference budgets.

R1.justification: Section 2's research positioning and the cited works remain unchanged after matching updated author lists, dates and publication metadata. Apparent replacements such as the Gemini 2.5 and gpt-oss references identify the same works.

P1.justification: v4 expands the visual-input discussion, inserts a Layout Complexity Analysis appendix and an Impact Statement, and updates publication, acknowledgment and cross-reference text. Most existing prose and the overall narrative organization are retained.

P2.justification: v4 adds the rendering comparison in Figure 4 and Tables 3, 6 and 11, expands the error table with resource columns, and narrows the earlier tool/rendering table. Running headers and pagination change, while existing plots, illustrations and the basic layout are retained.

improvement.justification: Tables 3 and 11 more directly test dependence on symbolic coordinates, while Appendix E and Table 9 add useful difficulty and resource diagnostics. These strengthen an already complete benchmark. Benefits are partly offset by removed GPT-4.1-mini tool results, unclear Mixed-sample composition and overgeneralized visual-benefit prose: Table 11 shows GPT-5-mini Shortest Path falling from 53.5% to 52.0% with GenImg+JSON.
